photos.question: A client is receiving the first IV dose of amphotericin B. Which reaction is most common during the infusion?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #364!

🔥 This antifungal is famous for a nickname nursing students never forget. Do you know why?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Fever, chills and shaking

🧠 Rationale: Amphotericin B often causes infusion reactions within the first hours.

Fever, chills and rigors are the classic signs.

Premedication and a slow infusion help prevent them.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Amphotericin B

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Antifungal (polyene)

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Serious systemic fungal infections

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Fever, chills, rigors

🔹 Kidney damage (nephrotoxicity)

🔹 Low potassium and magnesium

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Premedicate as ordered (acetaminophen, diphenhydramine)

✅ Monitor kidney function and electrolytes

✅ Infuse slowly, check vitals often

✅ Watch intake and output

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Amphotericin B = "shake and bake" (chills and fever)!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Pharmacology #Antifungal #MedSafety #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse hears an S3 heart sound in a 70-year-old client. What does this finding most often suggest?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #365!

👂 Lub-dub-DUB. That extra sound could mean trouble. Do you know what it means?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Fluid overload or heart failure

🧠 Rationale: An S3 happens when blood rushes into a stiff or overfilled ventricle.

In older adults it usually signals heart failure or fluid overload.

It can be normal in children, young adults and pregnancy.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: S3 Heart Sound

❤️ What It Is:

🔹 Extra sound right after S2

🔹 Sounds like "Ken-tuc-ky"

🔹 Also called a ventricular gallop

⚠️ Linked To:

🔹 Heart failure

🔹 Fluid volume overload

🔹 Mitral regurgitation

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Listen at the apex with the bell

✅ Check lung sounds for crackles

✅ Check daily weight and edema

✅ Report new S3 to the provider

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

S3 = "Ken-tuc-ky" = too much fluid in the tank!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Cardiac #HeartSounds #HeartFailure #Assessment #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client has a large pleural effusion on the right side. Which finding should the nurse expect on that side?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #366!

🫁 Fluid around the lung changes everything you hear. Can you pick the right finding?

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Dullness and decreased breath sounds

🧠 Rationale: Fluid in the pleural space muffles sound and blocks airflow.

Percussion is dull and breath sounds are decreased or absent.

Hyperresonance points to air, as in a pneumothorax.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Pleural Effusion

🫁 What It Is:

🔹 Extra fluid between lung and chest wall

❤️ Common Causes:

🔹 Heart failure

🔹 Pneumonia

🔹 Cancer

🔹 Kidney or liver disease

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Shortness of breath

🔹 Dull percussion

🔹 Decreased breath sounds and fremitus

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Raise the head of the bed

✅ Give oxygen as ordered

✅ Prepare for thoracentesis

✅ Monitor SpO2 and breathing

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Fluid = Flat and dull. Air = hyper and loud!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: The nurse teaches a client about subcutaneous insulin. Which site usually absorbs insulin the fastest?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #367!

💉 Not all injection sites work at the same speed. Which one wins the race?

This is a HIGH-YIELD endocrine question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Abdomen

🧠 Rationale: The abdomen absorbs subcutaneous insulin the fastest.

The arm is next, then the thigh and buttock.

Rotating within one area keeps absorption more predictable.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Insulin Injection Sites

💉 Absorption Order:

🔹 Abdomen (fastest)

🔹 Upper arm

🔹 Thigh

🔹 Buttock (slowest)

⚠️ Problems to Avoid:

🔹 Lipohypertrophy from same-spot injections

🔹 Injecting into scars or bruises

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Rotate sites within one area

✅ Stay 2 inches away from the navel

✅ Check glucose as instructed

✅ Exercise can speed absorption from a limb

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

A is for Abdomen and A is for Absorbs fastest!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Endocrine #Diabetes #Insulin #PatientTeaching #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: Why are tetracycline antibiotics usually avoided in children younger than 8 years?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #368!

🦷 This antibiotic can leave a lasting mark on a child's smile. Do you know why?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Permanent tooth staining

🧠 Rationale: Tetracyclines bind to calcium in developing teeth and bones.

This can cause permanent yellow or brown tooth staining.

Doxycycline may still be used short term for some serious infections.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Tetracyclines in Children

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Tetracyclines (tetracycline, doxycycline, minocycline)

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Tooth staining in young children

🔹 Sun sensitivity

🔹 GI upset

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Avoid in pregnancy and under age 8 unless prescribed

✅ Do not take with milk, antacids or iron

✅ Use sunscreen and limit sun

✅ Take with a full glass of water

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Tetracycline + Tots = Tinted Teeth!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: The nurse is timing a laboring client's contractions. How is the frequency of contractions measured?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #369!

⏱️ Timing contractions sounds easy, but many students mix this up. Do you know the rule?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — From the start of one to the start of the next

🧠 Rationale: Frequency is timed from the start of one contraction to the start of the next.

Duration is timed from the start to the end of one contraction.

Contractions closer than every 2 minutes need follow-up.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Timing Contractions

⏱️ Key Terms:

🔹 Frequency: start to start

🔹 Duration: start to end

🔹 Intensity: strength at the peak

⚠️ Report Right Away:

🔹 Contractions more often than every 2 minutes

🔹 Contractions lasting over 90 seconds

🔹 No rest between contractions

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Palpate the fundus or use the monitor

✅ Check fetal heart rate with contractions

✅ Stop oxytocin if contractions are too frequent

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Frequency = Start to Start. Duration = Start to Stop!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Maternity #LaborAndDelivery #OBNursing #Contractions #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client says, "I'm worried about going home." Which response by the nurse uses reflection?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #370!

🗣️ Therapeutic communication shows up everywhere on the NCLEX. Can you spot the right technique?

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — "You're worried about going home?"

🧠 Rationale: Reflection repeats the client's feelings back so the client can explore them.

False reassurance and changing the subject shut down talking.

"Why" questions can make clients feel defensive.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Therapeutic Communication

✅ Therapeutic Techniques:

🔹 Reflection: repeat feelings back

🔹 Open-ended questions

🔹 Active listening and silence

🔹 Clarifying

⚠️ Nontherapeutic Responses:

🔹 False reassurance

🔹 "Why" questions

🔹 Changing the subject

🔹 Giving advice

🚨 NCLEX Strategy:

✅ Pick the answer that focuses on feelings

✅ Keep the focus on the client

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Reflect it back like a mirror: feelings first!
